title: DeFoe
summary: DeFoe was a scheming, self-proclaimed mastermind. He lead a small force for the Organization alongside his right-hand man, Grier, under orders to track down a journal in Lok’s possession and to halt the actions of the Huntik Foundation against them. He would stop at nothing to see that his missions were completed, although sometimes this meant putting his own men in peril to do so.

sections.heading: History
sections.text:
]]
Little is known about DeFoe's background, but his rocket-like rise through the Organization hierarchy is legendary amongst Suits. Within a matter of months, DeFoe was promoted through Suit rankings to be a prominent leader of his own squad. [Huntik.com]

Under the Professor, one of DeFoe's earlier missions was to retrieve Eathon Lambert's journal, although the mission ended with the journal being all but destroyed. [A Seeker Is Born] DeFoe then ordered Grier to find the biggest Venice Huntik Library because he knew that the Huntik team needed to research Eathon's journal. DeFoe later attacked the library, breaking through by pouring acid on the door's knob. Though he failed to retrieve the journal he manages to learn the Huntik team's next move. [The Casterwill Client]

After DeFoe learned that the Huntik team is going to Prague, Czech Republic, to get the Titan Metagolem he ambushed the Huntik team when they were going to retrieve the Jodis Lore's Key, He successfully obtained the key and went to the Golem's Attic, Where he tried to bond with the Titan Metagolem but failed due to Dante's interference so DeFoe retreated because Dante had bonded with Metagolem. [Words of Truth, Heart of Lies]
]]
Afterwards, DeFoe's team was sent to retrieve the Amulets of the re-awakening Titans. In the Cave of the Gargoyle on the outskirts of Rouen, France, DeFoe managed to retrieve and bond with Gar-Ghoul. [Into the River of Secrets]. DeFoe then was ordered by the Professor to retrieve the Ring of Arc. He then had a rematch between Dante's Caliban and DeFoe's "new friend," his Gar-Ghoul, but Dante fled with the other's to the catacombs. [Crawling the Catacombs] DeFoe pursued the team, intent on obtaining the Ring of Arc, but failed due to Dante's plan, dividing up his forces and sneaking the Ring past them using Gareon. Because of this failure, he was removed from his duties, by Rassimov as the Professor was too furious to lay eyes on him. DeFoe then swore to bring Dante's end with or without the Organization. [Divide and Conquer]

His removal was temporary, as he was later reinstated by Rassimov after nearly destroying the Organization's training machine while training. DeFoe was then given a mission to retrieve the Amulet of King Basilisk, but he again failed due to the intervention of Dante's team. [Absent Heroes]

DeFoe was then ordered simply to deliver the Sword of Saint George to Prague, Czech Republic. The Sword contained the Titan Lindorm, but the Organization considered DeFoe to be unworthy to bond with the Titan. Unsatisfied at simply being a "delivery boy," he went to Greece after receiving word from his spies that Dante Vale was sighted there in order to kill Dante. DeFoe, however, failed, resulting in Lok bonding with Lindorm and DeFoe's Amulets being taken by the Huntik Foundation. [The Treasures of the Argonauts] 
]]
Having been removed from his duties, DeFoe planned to to use his operative access to steal a number of Titans from the Organization for his revenge on Dante Vale. However, he was murdered by his own right-hand man, Grier, by order of the Professor, who thought Defoe to be incapable of carrying out his orders.[The Beautiful Trap] 

Whilst attempting to reason with Wilder, Sophie told him she had thought him to be different from DeFoe or Klaus, because of his talk of uniting people, to which Wilder said they were just "protecting the status quo". Grier later implied his killing of DeFoe to be a reason for him to stay on Sutos Island and not join the Huntik Foundation, telling Dante that he had done a lot of things that he was not proud of to reach his position. [An Ally from the Organization]

sections.heading: Personality
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S1E01 DeFoe.png|thumb|200px]]
Known for his high expectations, efficiency, and sadistic obsession with acid and many different kinds of poisons, DeFoe is feared by friend and foe alike, he also has a slippery habit of escaping and leaving his suits to do his dirty work for him from time to time. He seems to look down upon his subordinates.  He harbors a strong and obsessive hatred for Dante Vale, being willing to put a mission at risk to defeat him. Dante stated that he himself does not know the reason for DeFoe's grudge, but DeFoe will try anything, even if it endangers his mission, to kill Dante Vale. {{source|Words of Truth, Heart of Lies}} He also seems to have a huge ego, and thinks he is better than others, due to his having an easy life, as stated by Zhalia. {{source|Divide and Conquer}} But he does not have much in the way of fight skills and that more than likely contributes to his failures against Dante Vale. Also he appears to be impulsive, as evidenced by his attack on Dante Vale, when Dante, Zhalia, Lok, Sophie and Cherit were exploring the sunken ship from the Argo Fleet. He also seems to hold his grudge against Dante Vale above his missions. {{Source|The Treasures of the Argonauts}} He apparenly also throws temper tantrums when things don't go his way, as shown when Grier carried him away {{Source|The Treasures of the Argonauts}}.

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.wikitext:
[[File:Defoe_Amulets.png|thumb|250px|DeFoe's [[Amulets]]]]
With endless hatred, DeFoe pursues Dante and friends using his squad of Suit operatives and his own Seeker abilities. His choice spells are an array of acidic and poisonous powers, and [[Kreutalk]], his signature [[Titan]], is capable of burning through anything in its way with the venomous acid it spits. In addition to his powers, DeFoe typically carried a silver vial of acid that he would often use to threaten his enemies up close. {{source|Absent Heroes}} He possessed a number of Titans, and, in some cases, several Amulets of the same Titan, as seen in his bag. {{source|The Treasures of the Argonauts}}

sections.heading: Bonded Titans
sections.text:
Gar-Ghoul — TV Series — taken — Found in the Cave of the Gargoyle; it was unbonded by Dante using Sorrowbond and secretly claimed by Zhalia Moon.

Icarus — TV Series — taken — An Icarus Amulet was seen amongst DeFoe's collection; it was unbonded by Dante and taken to the Huntik Foundation.

Kreutalk x2 — TV Series — taken — DeFoe's Signature Titan who shared his obsession with acid. Two Kreutalk Amulets were seen in his collection; both were unbonded by Dante and taken to the Foundation.

Mindrone x2 — TV Series — taken — Two Mindrone Amulets were seen in DeFoe's collection; both were unbonded by Dante and taken to the Foundation.

Redcap x3 — TV Series — taken — Three Redcap Amulets were seen in DeFoe's collection; all three were unbonded by Dante and taken to the Foundation.

Bonelasher — TCG — taken — DeFoe was shown to possess a Bonelasher; unbonded by Dante and taken to the Foundation.

Unnamed Titan 011 — TCG — taken — An Egpytian-themed reptile man; unbonded by Dante and taken to the Foundation.

Unnamed Titan 012 — TCG — taken — A teal scarab-like Titan; unbonded by Dante and taken to the Foundation.

Unnamed Titan 013 — TCG — taken — A purple-skinned Yama-Titan armed with a scimitar; unbonded by Dante and taken to the Foundation.
